input.title: scheduled backup job
input.behavior: Every night at 02:00 a backup agent reads a large set of files and uploads to the on-prem backup server over the dedicated backup VLAN; the volume is consistent with the previous 60 days.

input.title: authorized vuln scan
input.behavior: A scanner appliance from the security team's subnet scanned a range of internal hosts on common ports; the scan pattern matches the quarterly authorized scan calendar and the appliance is whitelisted.

input.title: orchestrated deployment
input.behavior: The deployment orchestrator pushed an update to 40 servers in waves; each server ran the installer, restarted a service, and reported back; the package hash matches the approved release.

input.title: internal DNS monitor
input.behavior: The DNS monitoring sensor resolves a long list of internal and external domains at high volume every 5 minutes as part of its normal operation; queries originate from the sensor's dedicated account.

input.title: CI pipeline agent
input.behavior: A CI runner cloned repos, executed tests, and published build artifacts; it authenticates with a service account and its network fingerprint is stable across the last 6 months.

input.title: authorized red-team exercise
input.behavior: A red-team operator with a temporary authorized account used a C2-style toolset against a scoped test range; the engagement is in the approved calendar and the operator's badge is recorded.

input.title: CDN/WAF traffic noise
input.behavior: The CDN edge forwards a high volume of mixed requests including a small number of probes that are immediately blocked by the WAF with 403s; the blocked probes are consistent with internet-wide background noise.

input.title: developer debug session
input.behavior: A developer connected to the staging database, ran a set of ad-hoc queries including a few that look like enumeration, and pulled a config file to reproduce a bug; the session is on the developer's machine with their normal account.

input.title: admin PowerShell automation
input.behavior: A known administrator account ran a signed PowerShell script from a change-request ticket during the maintenance window; the script enumerated services and set a scheduled task for the nightly backup.

input.title: repeated logon failures then success
input.behavior: A single source IP attempted logon with many distinct usernames over 90 seconds, several account lockouts, then a successful logon with a newly created account followed by a sensitive share access.

input.title: obfuscated script execution chain
input.behavior: A document dropped an encoded script that decoded to a PowerShell one-liner, which downloaded a binary from a rarely-seen domain, and the binary then ran with an unusual parent process tree.

input.title: startup persistence write
input.behavior: A process wrote a registry Run key and created a scheduled task pointing to an executable in the user profile directory, both configured to start at logon.

input.title: remote admin service usage
input.behavior: From a compromised workstation an account connected to three servers using an administrative service, executed a remote command on each, and then the same account appeared on the domain controller minutes later.

input.title: beaconing to dynamic domain
input.behavior: A host made periodic HTTPS connections every 55-65 seconds to a newly registered domain with no historical DNS records; responses had an unusual TLS fingerprint and payload sizes were uniform.

input.title: bulk archive upload
input.behavior: An endpoint compressed a large set of documents it had never accessed before into a single archive and uploaded it to a file-sharing domain outside the org, in one burst at night.

input.title: privilege escalation via new access key
input.behavior: An identity that normally logs in from a single office region suddenly authenticated from an unexpected region, created a new access key, attached an admin policy to a role it does not own, and began enumerating secrets.

input.title: privileged pod with host mount
input.behavior: A pod was created with privileged=true and the host filesystem mounted; inside it a process wrote to a host directory and started a shell listening on a host network port.

input.title: intrusion chain across hosts
input.behavior: A phishing attachment executed a script, which downloaded a remote access tool; the tool enumerated the network, moved to another server over an admin service, dumped credentials, and then compressed data for upload.

input.title: public web server request pattern

input.behavior: A host made periodic HTTPS connections every 55-65 seconds to a newly registered domain with no historical DNS records; responses had an unusual TLS fingerprint and payload sizes were uniform.

input.title: bulk archive upload
input.behavior: An endpoint compressed a large set of documents it had never accessed before into a single archive and uploaded it to a file-sharing domain outside the org, in one burst at night.

input.title: privilege escalation via new access key
input.behavior: An identity that normally logs in from a single office region suddenly authenticated from an unexpected region, created a new access key, attached an admin policy to a role it does not own, and began enumerating secrets.

input.title: privileged pod with host mount
input.behavior: A pod was created with privileged=true and the host filesystem mounted; inside it a process wrote to a host directory and started a shell listening on a host network port.

input.title: intrusion chain across hosts
input.behavior: A phishing attachment executed a script, which downloaded a remote access tool; the tool enumerated the network, moved to another server over an admin service, dumped credentials, and then compressed data for upload.

input.title: public web server request pattern
input.behavior: Multiple requests to /login with sql-like fragments and encoded payloads, followed by a request writing a small php file under a web-accessible path, then a callback to an external host.
